sops.title: Hydraulic Pressure Below Setpoint Warning
sops.condition: The hydraulic pressure sensor reads between the low-pressure warning threshold and the critical alarm floor while the press is actively cycling.

sops.title: Sudden Hydraulic Pressure Collapse During Cycle
sops.condition: Hydraulic system pressure drops instantaneously to below ten percent of the operating setpoint while the ram is mid-stroke under forming load.

sops.title: Hydraulic Pressure Exceeds Maximum Rated Ceiling
sops.condition: The hydraulic pressure sensor reading exceeds the system maximum rated operating pressure alarm threshold, indicating runaway pressure build-up.

sops.title: Ram Descent Velocity Below Specified Rate
sops.condition: The ram is descending but at a speed measurably slower than the programmed cycle time tolerance, with no full stop occurring.

sops.title: Ram Completely Stalled at Mid-Stroke Position
sops.condition: The ram has ceased all movement at an intermediate position and will not advance or retract in response to any control input.

sops.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Elevated Above Normal Range
sops.condition: The oil temperature sensor reading exceeds the normal operating upper limit but remains below the automatic shutdown interlock threshold, and the press continues to run.

sops.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Triggers Automatic Shutdown Interlock
sops.condition: Oil temperature exceeds the automatic shutdown interlock setpoint, causing the press control system to disable the hydraulic pump and halt all press motion.

sops.title: Minor Hydraulic Oil Seep at Fitting or Cylinder Seal
sops.condition: A slow drip or surface seep of hydraulic oil is detected at a hose fitting, connection, or cylinder seal with no floor pooling observed.

sops.title: High-Pressure Hydraulic Hose Rupture and Oil Spray
sops.condition: A hydraulic hose or pressurized fitting fails catastrophically, producing high-velocity oil spray or rapid large-volume oil discharge that reaches the floor or surrounding equipment.

sops.title: Pressure Relief Valve Rapid Cycling Under Load
sops.condition: The hydraulic relief valve is audibly and measurably cycling open and closed in rapid succession while the press operates under normal forming load.

sops.title: Hydraulic Pump Motor Thermal Overload Trip
sops.condition: The hydraulic pump motor thermal overload relay has tripped, cutting power to the pump and halting all hydraulic flow.

sops.title: Ram Position Sensor Signal Lost or Erratic
sops.condition: The ram position encoder or proximity sensor generates an out-of-range, intermittent, or frozen signal that triggers a position fault alarm on the press controller.

sops.title: Scheduled Hydraulic Oil Filter Element Replacement
sops.condition: The hydraulic filter differential-pressure indicator reaches the scheduled change threshold or the planned preventive maintenance interval has elapsed.

sops.title: Hydraulic Reservoir Oil Level Inspection and Top-Off
sops.condition: The reservoir oil level sight glass reads below the minimum operating mark during a routine daily inspection, with no sign of oil degradation.

sops.title: Complete Hydraulic Oil Drain Flush and Refill
sops.condition: The scheduled full oil-change interval has been reached or oil analysis results indicate fluid degradation beyond acceptable contamination limits.

sops.title: Hydraulic Pump Drive Coupling Grease Application
sops.condition: The scheduled lubrication interval for the pump drive coupling has elapsed per the preventive maintenance calendar.

sops.title: Hydraulic Oil Cooler Heat Exchanger Cleaning
sops.condition: The temperature differential across the oil cooler exceeds the inspection threshold or the scheduled cleaning interval has elapsed, indicating fouled cooler fins.

sops.title: Pressure Relief Valve Setpoint Testing and Adjustment
sops.condition: The scheduled relief-valve calibration interval has elapsed or a maintenance work order has been raised following a pressure anomaly event requiring setpoint verification.

sops.title: Hydraulic Press Lockout Tagout Energy Isolation
sops.condition: A maintenance or repair task requires entry into the press hazard zone or physical contact with any hydraulic or electrical component.

sops.title: Hydraulic Oil Spill Containment and Cleanup
sops.condition: Hydraulic oil is observed pooling on the floor in any quantity sufficient to create a slip hazard or approach a floor drain.

sops.title: Emergency Stop Activation and Press Safe-Down Procedure
sops.condition: An e-stop button has been activated by any person due to an immediate safety hazard at or near the hydraulic press.

sops.title: Daily Press Startup and End-of-Shift Shutdown Sequence
sops.condition: The press is being placed into or removed from normal production service at the start or end of a scheduled shift.

incidents.text: Been watching the gauge on press 4 all morning shift — needle's sitting about 15 bar below where it should be but she's still cycling. Nothing tripped, no alarm, just soft. Wanted to flag it before second shift takes over.

Line 2 stamping cell, the readout on the main panel is running below the green zone. Machine kept right on running through the whole shift. Not making any funny noise, just consistently under where we'd expect it. Tech needs to take a look.

We were punching blanks on the line 3 press, right in the middle of a stroke, and the whole system just lost it in under a second. Ram froze halfway down. Nothing slow about it — the gauge just fell to the floor instantly.

Heard a kind of whomp from the far press bay on second shift. Operator said the gauge dropped to nothing while they were mid-form — didn't gradually trend down, literally gone in a blink. Part was stuck under the tooling.

Press 7 near the loading dock dropped out completely during a forming cycle. System went from full operating pressure to basically zero while the ram was loaded — not a slow bleed, a total instant loss. Called it in right away.
Alarm went off on the big press near the loading dock — the gauge is pegged past the red line. Machine was still trying to cycle. Shift lead cleared everyone back from the area fast.
Second shift, line 1 — pressure reading is higher than I've ever seen on that unit. Pump is humming loud and the needle is buried past the maximum mark on the dial. Something's not venting.

The panel on press 5 lit up red during a run. When I walked over the gauge was way into the danger zone — far above anything normal. Nowhere near the low end, completely the opposite. Had to stop production.

The ram on press 5 is still going down but it's taking almost twice as long to reach the bottom of stroke. Parts are stacking up because the cycle just drags. Never actually stopped, just real sluggish.

Line 4 has been running lazy all morning shift. Ram is definitely moving — you can see it creeping down — but takt time is way off. Supervisor noticed the count was behind and I went to check. The descent just takes forever.
Press 3 locked up on us mid-stroke. The ram is just sitting there about halfway down, won't go forward, won't come back up. Tried the selector switch, tried cycling the mode — nothing responds.

The unit by the loading dock froze up completely on third shift. Part's still under the tooling and nothing is moving. It's not slow — it is completely stopped. Operator couldn't get it to move in either direction.

Line 6 press jammed solid about midway through the down-stroke. Ram is stuck between top and bottom, just hanging there. Different from when it runs slow — this thing is not moving at all, and it won't retract either.

Temp on the reservoir for press bay 2 was reading orange on the display but the press never stopped on its own. Maintenance lead told the operator to keep an eye on it. Machine was still making parts — just running hot.

End of day shift on line 3, noticed the oil temp number was creeping up past the normal band on the display. Fan looked like it was spinning. The machine was still operational and the interlock never kicked. Just hotter than usual.

Press bay 2 killed itself on third shift — came in and the pump was dead quiet, big red fault on the panel, and the whole machine was locked out. Reservoir was so hot you could feel the heat standing a foot away from it.

Line 5 press shut down by itself during a stamping run. No one hit E-stop — the machine just went offline. Temp gauge was buried and the interlock had already tripped everything off. Had to call maintenance right away.

Spotted a wet fitting on press 6 near the cylinder block — just a small bead of fluid running down the hose. No puddle on the floor yet. Put a rag under it and flagged it for the next maintenance window.

There's a weep at one of the connections on the back of press 2. Maybe a drip every few seconds — you'd miss it if you weren't looking. Floor underneath is dry. Definitely not right though, and I wrote it up.
First shift, line 3 — a hose let go completely. Fluid was spraying across the bay, hit the guarding and the floor. Had to push everyone back fast. Big spreading puddle within seconds of it blowing.

The high-pressure line on press bay 4 blew out mid-cycle. We're talking a jet, not a drip — covered the floor and got on the operator's PPE. Nothing gradual about it. Press area is completely shut down.

Press 8 near the south wall threw a hose during a forming run. The spray was strong enough to reach the adjacent conveyor. Floor is flooded. Nothing like the little weeps we see sometimes — this was a full blowout.

There's this fast clicking noise coming from the press bay near the pump — like a valve ticking 10 times a second. Pressure needle is bouncing. Nothing else obvious wrong, machine is still under load.

Line 6 press sounds like a machine gun when it gets under load. The tech said it's the relief valve hammering back and forth. Only happens when we're stamping the heavier blanks. Pressure gauge is oscillating fast.

Motor control cabinet for press 1 tripped out and the pump went completely quiet. No alarm sounded — it just died. When the tech checked, the reset button was popped on the overload relay inside the cabinet.
Third shift — pump motor on line 2 cut out mid-run. The MCC breaker looks fine when you check it, but the overload is tripped and the machine won't restart. Hydraulics are flat, nothing moving.

Press 4 keeps throwing a fault alarm on the controller even when the ram is sitting still at the top of stroke. The position display on the panel is jumping all over the place — numbers don't make sense.

Line 3 started giving erratic stroke counts — the encoder readout is flickering between two different values and the press stopped itself. Electrician thinks the sensor is flaking out. Controls faulted, not hydraulics.
PM schedule said the filter on press 2 was due last Friday. The bypass indicator on the housing is in the red this morning. Maintenance flagged it at the start of first shift and ordered the element.

The differential indicator on the filter housing of the line 4 press has been amber for a full week. This week's PM interval crossed over so the element needs swapping out — no fault yet but it's overdue.
Routine walkaround this morning on press 3 — the sight glass is right below the low mark. Nothing urgent, just needs a top-up before first shift gets into full production.
Line 1 press reservoir is visibly low in the glass during the daily check. Last topped off two weeks ago. Oil looks fine, just low on volume. Needs maybe a quart or two to bring it back to the mark.

Oil analysis came back on the line 5 press and the contamination numbers are way too high for continued service. Lab report says change out the whole system — not just the filter, a full flush and fresh fill.

The PM counter on press bay 3 hit the full-change milestone this quarter. Oil looks dark and the tech said it smells burnt when you pull the dipstick. Whole system needs draining — topping off won't cut it this time.
Maintenance log shows the coupling grease on press 1 pump is six months overdue. Could hear a faint squeal coming from that area on second shift — caught it early before it gets worse.

Line 6 PM inspection — the lube sticker on the pump coupling guard still shows last year's date. Calendar says this month is the interval. No complaint from the machine yet but it's definitely time to grease it.
Oil temp on line 4 press has been creeping up week over week even when the shop isn't particularly hot. Tech pulled the cooler shroud and the fins are completely packed with dust and metal fines.
The cooler on press bay 2 looks like it hasn't been touched in over a year — fins are black with debris. The temperature difference across it during production is way off what it should be.
Work order came in after last month's pressure event on line 3 press. The relief valve needs its annual setpoint verification before we can close the corrective action and sign off on the machine.
PM calendar flag on press 5 — the setpoint check is overdue by two weeks. No current problem to report, just the scheduled verification cycle. Tech needs to pull the calibrated gauge and do the test.

Maintenance is going into press 2 to replace a cylinder seal. Before anyone touches it the electrician is pulling the LOTO kit from the cabinet — can't have stored energy in the system while someone's in there.
Second shift, line 6 — tech needs to get inside the tooling area to clear a stuck blank. Can't do anything until we have full energy isolation on the machine. Hasp goes on before anyone reaches in.

Inspection crew needs to remove the cylinder guard on press 4 for a scheduled internal check. Job safety analysis says full isolation before any guard removal — pulling the tag kit now before work starts.

There's a puddle of hydraulic fluid spreading across the aisle between press bay 3 and press bay 4. Started small but it's big enough to be a slip hazard. Someone put a cone out but we need the spill kit.

Came in first thing on day shift and found a trail of oil from press 1 all the way toward the floor drain. Big enough that one of the operators nearly went down. Area is roped off and safety needs to know.

Operator on line 5 hit the mushroom button when a blank misloaded and they weren't sure their hand was clear. Machine stopped hard. Everything is locked out. Need a full inspection before it gets released.
Someone hit the big red on press bay 1 — saw a worker step into the light curtain zone during a run. Machine locked out immediately. Safety officer and shift lead need to clear it before restart.

The E-stop on press 7 was smacked by a forklift bumping the guarding — machine tripped offline. Nobody was hurt, but the system is in fault state and the ram position needs to be verified before we can do anything.

First shift coming on for press 3 — previous shift left it powered down for the long weekend. Need to do the full warmup walkthrough: pressure build, temp stabilization, level check before we start punching parts.

End of Friday second shift on line 2. Shutting down for the weekend. Need to go through the safe-down sequence properly before facilities locks up the building — can't just kill the main breaker and walk out.
